+; CHECK-NEXT:    call void @fn_read_inaccessible_mem(i32 [[LOAD]])

+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP:%.*]] = icmp ult i32 [[ACC]], 10

+; CHECK:       [[AFTER_LOOP]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[ACC_LCSSA:%.*]] = phi i32 [ [[ACC]], %[[LOOP]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i32 [[ACC_LCSSA]]
+;

+  br label %loop
+loop:
+  %phi = phi ptr [ %start, %entry ], [ %gep, %loop ]

steps.subject: [LICM] Improve hoist-safety checks for dominated MemorySSA accesses (#169379)

evidence: Directly changes LICM noConflictingReadWrites to use MSSA->dominates(IMD, &MA), the same dominance mechanism implicated by the OtherClobbers assertion.
The failing stack reaches canHoistLoad, hoistRegion, LICMPass, and the MemorySSA clobber walker; this patch changes which accesses LICM ignores while making those decisions.
features: clobber-walker-adjacent, licm-hoist-safety, loop-mssa, memoryssa-dominance, meta:core-llvm, path:llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This LICM change refines MemorySSA-backed hoist-safety checking. In noConflictingReadWrites, when LICM is considering hoisting rather than sinking, it now ignores an examined MemorySSA access if the candidate instruction's memory access IMD dominates that access. The accompanying tests explicitly expand which inaccessible-memory writes LICM may hoist while retaining a case where a potentially conflicting inaccessible-memory read prevents hoisting.
Changed symbols: noConflictingReadWrites; LICMPass::run (MemorySSA execution context shown); loop_alias (new LICM regression test); ne_loop_alias (new LICM regression test)
Behavioral change: Changes noConflictingReadWrites so that, for a hoist operation, an access MA dominated by IMD is skipped before conflict processing: if (!Flags.getIsSink() && MSSA->dominates(IMD, &MA)) continue.; Changes which MemorySSA accesses participate in LICM's conflicting-read/write safety decision and can consequently allow additional hoisting.; Adds tests expecting LICM to hoist an inaccessible-memory writer when the remaining accesses do not conflict, while preserving a non-hoist case with a conflicting inaccessible-memory reader.
Assertion or trace link: MSSA->dominates(IMD, &MA) is directly added in the changed LICM safety logic.; The failure assertion is also a MemorySSA dominance invariant: every OtherClobbers entry must dominate the primary clobber.; The supplied stack includes canHoistLoad, hoistRegion, LICMPass::run, and MemorySSA::ClobberWalkerBase::getClobberingMemoryAccessBase.
Reproducer link: The added regression test runs opt -passes='loop-mssa(licm)' and exercises LICM hoisting decisions involving calls with inaccessible-memory effects.; The reported reduced C testcase and its exact memory-access/control-flow pattern are not present, so an exact reproducer match cannot be established.
Pass or subsystem link: LICM; loop-mssa; MemorySSA; MemorySSA dominance reasoning
Causal explanation: This is a close causal candidate because it directly changes LICM's use of MemorySSA dominance while deciding whether a memory operation is safe to hoist, and the crash occurs during LICM hoisting in a MemorySSA clobber-walker dominance verification. Skipping dominated accesses changes the conflict set used by LICM and may change which hoists and subsequent MemorySSA queries occur. The patch does not modify ClobberWalker::verifyOptResult or MemorySSA updating directly, so the retrieved evidence does not prove whether it introduces or fixes the invalid clobber ordering; it does, however, identify a direct shared mechanism and execution path.

Summary: This LICM change refines MemorySSA-backed hoist-safety checking. In noConflictingReadWrites, when LICM is considering hoisting rather than sinking, it now ignores an examined MemorySSA access if the candidate instruction's memory access IMD dominates that access. The accompanying tests explicitly expand which inaccessible-memory writes LICM may hoist while retaining a case where a potentially conflicting inaccessible-memory read prevents hoisting.
Changed symbols: noConflictingReadWrites; LICMPass::run (MemorySSA execution context shown); loop_alias (new LICM regression test); ne_loop_alias (new LICM regression test)
Behavioral change: Changes noConflictingReadWrites so that, for a hoist operation, an access MA dominated by IMD is skipped before conflict processing: if (!Flags.getIsSink() && MSSA->dominates(IMD, &MA)) continue.; Changes which MemorySSA accesses participate in LICM's conflicting-read/write safety decision and can consequently allow additional hoisting.; Adds tests expecting LICM to hoist an inaccessible-memory writer when the remaining accesses do not conflict, while preserving a non-hoist case with a conflicting inaccessible-memory reader.
Assertion or trace link: MSSA->dominates(IMD, &MA) is directly added in the changed LICM safety logic.; The failure assertion is also a MemorySSA dominance invariant: every OtherClobbers entry must dominate the primary clobber.; The supplied stack includes canHoistLoad, hoistRegion, LICMPass::run, and MemorySSA::ClobberWalkerBase::getClobberingMemoryAccessBase.
Reproducer link: The added regression test runs opt -passes='loop-mssa(licm)' and exercises LICM hoisting decisions involving calls with inaccessible-memory effects.; The reported reduced C testcase and its exact memory-access/control-flow pattern are not present, so an exact reproducer match cannot be established.
Pass or subsystem link: LICM; loop-mssa; MemorySSA; MemorySSA dominance reasoning
Causal explanation: This is a close causal candidate because it directly changes LICM's use of MemorySSA dominance while deciding whether a memory operation is safe to hoist, and the crash occurs during LICM hoisting in a MemorySSA clobber-walker dominance verification. Skipping dominated accesses changes the conflict set used by LICM and may change which hoists and subsequent MemorySSA queries occur. The patch does not modify ClobberWalker::verifyOptResult or MemorySSA updating directly, so the retrieved evidence does not prove whether it introduces or fixes the invalid clobber ordering; it does, however, identify a direct shared mechanism and execution path.
Causal confidence: 0.82
Build risk: Adds a focused loop-mssa(licm) regression test for inaccessible-memory call hoisting and a retained conflicting-access non-hoist case.; Updates LICM invariant.start output expectations, indicating changed LICM transformation behavior.; Updates MemorySSA analysis test expectations for existing PR tests, but no retrieved test explicitly enables the failing ClobberWalker verifyOptResult assertion on the reported -O1 reducer.

diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/LICM/hoist-inaccesiblemem-call.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/LICM/hoist-inaccesiblemem-call.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..03ab270de12e
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/LICM/hoist-inaccesiblemem-call.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,163 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --version 6
+; RUN: opt -passes='loop-mssa(licm)' < %s -S | FileCheck %s
+
+;; It should hoist fn_write_inaccessible_mem
+;; because there is no conflict between inaccessible memory
+;; fn_read_inaccessible_mem is a nice side effect
+define i32 @loop_alias(i64 %x, ptr %start) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define i32 @loop_alias(
+; CHECK-SAME: i64 [[X:%.*]], ptr [[START:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    call void @fn_write_inaccessible_mem()
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[LOOP:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[LOOP]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[PHI:%.*]] = phi ptr [ [[START]], %[[ENTRY]] ], [ [[GEP:%.*]], %[[LOOP]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[LOAD:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[PHI]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL:%.*]] = call i32 @fn_args(i32 [[LOAD]])
+; CHECK-NEXT:    call void @fn_read_inaccessible_mem(i32 [[LOAD]])
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP]] = getelementptr inbounds nuw i32, ptr [[PHI]], i64 [[X]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[ACC:%.*]] = add nuw nsw i32 [[VAL]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP:%.*]] = icmp ult i32 [[ACC]], 10
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP]], label %[[LOOP]], label %[[AFTER_LOOP:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[AFTER_LOOP]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[ACC_LCSSA:%.*]] = phi i32 [ [[ACC]], %[[LOOP]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i32 [[ACC_LCSSA]]
+;
+entry:
+  br label %loop
+loop:
+  %phi = phi ptr [ %start, %entry ], [ %gep, %loop ]
+  %load = load i32, ptr %phi
+  %val = call i32 @fn_args(i32 %load)
+  call void @fn_write_inaccessible_mem()
+  call void @fn_read_inaccessible_mem(i32 %load)
+  %gep = getelementptr inbounds nuw i32, ptr %phi, i64 %x
+  %acc = add nuw nsw i32 %val, 1
+  %cmp = icmp ult i32 %acc, 10
+  br i1 %cmp, label %loop, label %after_loop
+after_loop:
+  ret i32 %acc
+}
+
+;; It should NOT hoist fn_write_inaccessible_mem
+;; Because fn_read_inaccessible_mem_2 reads the same inaccessible memory
+define i32 @ne_loop_alias(i64 %x, ptr %start) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define i32 @ne_loop_alias(
+; CHECK-SAME: i64 [[X:%.*]], ptr [[START:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[LOOP:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[LOOP]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[PHI:%.*]] = phi ptr [ [[START]], %[[ENTRY]] ], [ [[GEP:%.*]], %[[LOOP]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[LOAD:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[PHI]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL:%.*]] = call i32 @fn_read_inaccessible_mem_2(i32 [[LOAD]])
+; CHECK-NEXT:    call void @fn_write_inaccessible_mem()
+; CHECK-NEXT:    call void @fn_read_inaccessible_mem(i32 [[VAL]])
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP]] = getelementptr inbounds nuw i32, ptr [[PHI]], i64 [[X]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[ACC:%.*]] = add nuw nsw i32 [[VAL]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP:%.*]] = icmp ult i32 [[ACC]], 10
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP]], label %[[LOOP]], label %[[AFTER_LOOP:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[AFTER_LOOP]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[ACC_LCSSA:%.*]] = phi i32 [ [[ACC]], %[[LOOP]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i32 [[ACC_LCSSA]]
+;
+entry:
+  br label %loop
+loop:
+  %phi = phi ptr [ %start, %entry ], [ %gep, %loop ]
+  %load = load i32, ptr %phi
+  %val = call i32 @fn_read_inaccessible_mem_2(i32 %load)
+  call void @fn_write_inaccessible_mem()
+  call void @fn_read_inaccessible_mem(i32 %val)
+  %gep = getelementptr inbounds nuw i32, ptr %phi, i64 %x
+  %acc = add nuw nsw i32 %val, 1
+  %cmp = icmp ult i32 %acc, 10
+  br i1 %cmp, label %loop, label %after_loop
+after_loop:
+  ret i32 %acc
+}
+
+;; Should hoist fn_write_inaccessible_mem
+;; It does not alias with store
+define void @hoist_untill_I(ptr noalias %loc, ptr noalias %loc2){
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @hoist_untill_I(
+; CHECK-SAME: ptr noalias [[LOC:%.*]], ptr noalias [[LOC2:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*:]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[LOC2]], align 4
+; CHECK-N

top_candidates.subject: Use auto for DenseMap/SmallDenseMap iterator variables. NFC (#196883)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This is a mechanical NFC cleanup replacing explicit DenseMap iterator declarations with auto at find() call sites. The retrieved changes affect MachineCombiner, legacy CallGraphSCCPass refresh logic, LoopIterator, ScalarEvolution, IRSimilarityIdentifier, and PeepholeOptimizer, without changing map operations, control flow, data flow, or pass behavior.
Changed symbols: llvm::MachineCombiner::getDepth; llvm::CGPassManager::RefreshCallGraph; llvm::LoopBlocksDFS::getPostorder; llvm::ScalarEvolution::getRangeRef; llvm::IRSimilarityIdentifier; llvm::PeepholeOptimizer::foldImmediate
Behavioral change: Explicit DenseMap::iterator and DenseMap::const_iterator local variable types are replaced by compiler-deduced auto types.; The find(), end(), dereference, and conditional logic in every visible hunk remain unchanged.
Assertion or trace link: ClobberWalker::verifyOptResult; MemorySSA::ClobberWalkerBase::getClobberingMemoryAccessBase; MSSA.dominates; llvm::LICMPass::run
Reproducer link: No visible hunk changes IR generation, memory-dependence reasoning, dominance, CFG mutation, or the clang -O1 pipeline.; The substitutions preserve the iterator types deduced from the same DenseMap::find expressions.
Pass or subsystem link: CodeGen MachineCombiner; legacy CGPassManager call-graph refresh; LoopIterator; ScalarEvolution; Not MemorySSA or the new-pass-manager LICM path in the crash trace
Causal explanation: Although one hunk is in call-graph pass infrastructure, it changes only the spelling of a local iterator type. The crash is a MemorySSA clobber-walker dominance assertion during LICM, and no retrieved change can alter the queried MemorySSA state or clobber result.
Causal confidence: 0.01
Build risk: The subject explicitly identifies the change as NFC, and the visible hunks support that characterization.; The edit spans several components, so ordinary compilation is needed to validate auto deduction in each context.; No test additions or MemorySSA-focused validation are present in the retrieved hunks.

@@ -7978,0 +7979,42 @@ See :ref:`Transformation Metadata <transformation-metadata>` for details.
+'``llvm.loop.vectorize.body``' Metadata
+^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
+
+This metadata is automatically added by the loop vectorizer to the
+vectorized loop body. It is used by subsequent optimization passes
+(such as the loop unroller and ``WarnMissedTransforms``) to emit more
+precise optimization remarks that identify the loop as a vector loop.
+
+The first operand is the string
+``llvm.loop.vectorize.body`` and the second operand is an
+integer. A value of 1 indicates this is a vectorized loop body:
+
+.. code-block:: llvm
+
+   !0 = !{!"llvm.loop.vectorize.body", i32 1}
+
+'``llvm.loop.vectorize.epilogue``' Metadata
+^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
+
+This metadata is automatically added by the loop vectorizer to the
+scalar remainder (epilogue) loop to identify it as such. It is used by
+subsequent optimization passes (such as the loop unroller and
+``WarnMissedTransforms``) to emit more precise optimization remarks
+that distinguish between the vectorized loop and its scalar remainder.
+
+Together these two attributes provide a four-way classification:
+
+- ``body`` only: main vectorized loop body
+- ``epilogue`` only: scalar epilogue loop after vectorization
+- Both ``body`` and ``epilogue``: vectorized epilogue 
+  (a remainder loop that was itself vectorized during epilogue
+  vectorization)
+- Neither: a plain loop not produced by the vectorizer
+
+The first operand is the string
+``llvm.loop.vectorize.epilogue`` and the second operand is
+an integer. A value of 1 indicates the loop is a remainder loop:
+
+.. code-block:: llvm
+
+   !0 = !{!"llvm.loop.vectorize.epilogue", i32 1}
+

index 06c5f433f6a5..f3e2f23475f2 100644
--- a/llvm/docs/LangRef.rst
+++ b/llvm/docs/LangRef.rst
@@ -7968,0 +7969,42 @@ See :ref:`Transformation Metadata <transformation-metadata>` for details.
+'``llvm.loop.vectorize.body``' Metadata
+^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
+
+This metadata is automatically added by the loop vectorizer to the
+vectorized loop body. It is used by subsequent optimization passes
+(such as the loop unroller and ``WarnMissedTransforms``) to emit more
+precise optimization remarks that identify the loop as a vector loop.
+
+The first operand is the string
+``llvm.loop.vectorize.body`` and the second operand is an
+integer. A value of 1 indicates this is a vectorized loop body:
+
+.. code-block:: llvm
+
+   !0 = !{!"llvm.loop.vectorize.body", i32 1}
+
+'``llvm.loop.vectorize.epilogue``' Metadata
+^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
+
+This metadata is automatically added by the loop vectorizer to the
+scalar remainder (epilogue) loop to identify it as such. It is used by
+subsequent optimization passes (such as the loop unroller and
+``WarnMissedTransforms``) to emit more precise optimization remarks
+that distinguish between the vectorized loop and its scalar remainder.
+
+Together these two attributes provide a four-way classification:
+
+- ``body`` only: main vectorized loop body
+- ``epilogue`` only: scalar epilogue loop after vectorization
+- Both ``body`` and ``epilogue``: vectorized epilogue 
+  (a remainder loop that was itself vectorized during epilogue
+  vectorization)
+- Neither: a plain loop not produced by the vectorizer
+
+The first operand is the string
+``llvm.loop.vectorize.epilogue`` and the second operand is
+an integer. A value of 1 indicates the loop is a remainder loop:
+
+.. code-block:: llvm
+
+   !0 = !{!"llvm.loop.vectorize.epilogue", i32 1}
+

+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[REF_TMP_SROA_0_0_INSERT_EXT:%.*]] = zext i32 [[_PRECISION]] to i64
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP0:%.*]] = inttoptr i64 [[REF_TMP_SROA_0_0_INSERT_EXT]] to ptr
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_I:%.*]] = icmp sgt i32 [[_PRECISION]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_I]], label %[[IF_THEN_I:.*]], label %[[IF_END_I]]
+; CHECK:       [[IF_THEN_I]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret { ptr, i32 } zeroinitializer
+; CHECK:       [[IF_END_I]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP1:%.*]] = phi ptr [ [[TMP0]], %[[IF_END16]] ], [ null, %[[ENTRY]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    call void @llvm.assume(i1 true) [ "align"(ptr [[TMP1]], i64 8), "nonnull"(ptr [[TMP1]]), "dereferenceable"(ptr [[TMP1]], i64 1) ]

+;

+

+  %0 = inttoptr i64 %ref.tmp.sroa.0.0.insert.ext to ptr

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: Refactors InstCombine handling of llvm.assume operand bundles around a new BundleAttr classification API. visitCallInst now switches on recognized bundle attributes, treats an unrecognized bundle as unreachable, uses structured helpers for align and nonnull bundles, and handles separate_storage by replacing hint uses with their underlying objects. The change also adds assume-bundle tests covering alignment bundles and offsets.
Changed symbols: InstCombinerImpl::visitCallInst; BundleAttr; getBundleAttrFromOBU; getNameFromBundleAttr; getBundleAttrFromString; AssumeAlignInfo; getAssumeAlignInfo; AssumeDereferenceableInfo
Behavioral change: InstCombine now classifies assume operand bundles through BundleAttr rather than directly matching tag strings and operand counts in visitCallInst.; An operand bundle classified as BundleAttr::None reaches llvm_unreachable("Unexpected Attribute") in this code path.; For align bundles, simplification now uses getAssumeAlignInfo and requires a valid alignment, a valid zero offset, and power-of-two alignment before attempting redundancy removal.; For nonnull bundles, simplification now uses getAssumeNonNullInfo and queries the extracted pointer directly.; For separate_storage bundles, InstCombine still canonicalizes operands to their underlying objects, now through getAssumeSeparateStorageInfo and the BundleAttr switch.; The new tests exercise retention or removal of align assumptions with constant and variable offsets.
Assertion or trace link: InstCombine is present in the recorded -O1 pass sequence before LICM.; The observed assertion is later in MemorySSA.cpp: ClobberWalker::verifyOptResult checks that OtherClobbers dominate the primary clobber.; The crash trace includes canHoistLoad and hoistRegion, indicating later LICM/MemorySSA-backed memory-dependence reasoning.
Reproducer link: The reproducer crashes at -O1, a pipeline that includes InstCombine and then LICM.; This change can alter the IR seen by later passes by preserving, simplifying, or canonicalizing llvm.assume bundles and separate_storage pointer hints.
Pass or subsystem link: InstCombine; llvm.assume operand bundles; AliasAnalysis-relevant separate_storage assumptions; MemorySSA-backed LICM
Causal explanation: This is a plausible indirect candidate: InstCombine runs in the failing optimization pipeline, and the changed handling of align, nonnull, and especially separate_storage assumptions can change pointer canonicalization and alias-relevant facts before LICM asks MemorySSA for clobbers. Such altered IR or alias information could expose an invalid clobber-walker result. However, the retrieved hunks do not modify MemorySSA, its updater, dominance maintenance, or the asserted verification condition, and they provide no reproducer containing llvm.assume bundles. The evidence therefore supports pipeline adjacency and an indirect AA/memory-dependence route, not a direct demonstrated cause.
Causal confidence: 0.28
Build risk: Introduces a new BundleAttr API and changes InstCombine's handling of all encountered assume operand bundles.; Adds llvm_unreachable for bundles classified as unhandled in this path, creating a distinct assertion/failure possibility for unexpected bundle kinds.; Changes canonicalization of separate_storage hints to underlying objects, which can affect downstream alias reasoning.; Adds InstCombine assume-bundle regression coverage, but no retrieved MemorySSA, LICM, or clobber-walker regression test.

The change also adds assume-bundle tests covering alignment bundles and offsets.

selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This revert removes LICM support for canonicalizing a chain of InsertElementInst operations so that a loop-invariant outer insertion can be moved ahead of variant inner insertions and hoisted. It deletes the helper that validates insertion indices and rewires the insert chain, as well as the hoistRegion call-site that invoked the helper before normal LICM processing.
Changed symbols: llvm::hoistRegion; getConstantInsertionIndex; hoistInsertPastInsert; InsertElementInst; MemorySSAUpdater

+; RUN: opt < %s -mtriple aarch64-- -passes=consthoist -S | FileCheck %s
+
+; The PHI node has some inbound edges with constants that originate from
+; basic blocks that aren't reachable from entry. Those could be tricky
+; to update when trying to find insertion points etc for a common base
+; constant.
+
+; The test case was added as a regression test to show that that we no longer
+; hit assertion failures about number of users updated/rebased. The workaround
+; is to ignore phi edges from basic blocks that aren't reachable from entry
+; when looking for candidate constants.
+
+define i64 @func(i1 %b0, i1 %b1) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define i64 @func(
+; CHECK-SAME: i1 [[B0:%.*]], i1 [[B1:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*:]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[B0]], label %[[BLOCK1:.*]], label %[[BLOCK2:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[BLOCK1]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CONST1:%.*]] = bitcast i64 4886718345 to i64
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[MERGE:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[BLOCK2]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[B1]], label %[[BLOCK3:.*]], label %[[MERGE]]
+; CHECK:       [[BLOCK3]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CONST:%.*]] = bitcast i64 4886718345 to i64
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[MERGE]]
+; CHECK:       [[UNREACHABLE1:.*]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[MERGE]]
+; CHECK:       [[UNREACHABLE2:.*]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[MERGE]]
+; CHECK:       [[MERGE]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[V:%.*]] = phi i64 [ 4886718345, %[[UNREACHABLE1]] ], [ 4886718345, %[[UNREACHABLE2]] ], [ [[CONST1]], %[[BLOCK1]] ], [ [[CONST]], %[[BLOCK3]] ], [ 0, %[[BLOCK2]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i64 [[V]]
+;
+entry:
+  br i1 %b0, label %block1, label %block2
+
+block1:
+  br label %merge
+
+block2:
+  br i1 %b1, label %block3, label %merge
+
+block3:
+  br label %merge
+
+unreachable1:
+  br label %merge
+
+unreachable2:
+  br label %merge
+
+merge:
+  %v = phi i64 [ 4886718345, %unreachable1 ], [ 4886718345, %unreachable2 ], [ 4886718345, %block1 ], [ 4886718345, %block3 ], [ 0, %block2 ]
+  ret i64 %v

Summary: This SimplifyCFG/TTI change makes switch lookup-table construction honor a target-provided minimum integer element width. SwitchReplacement now receives TargetTransformInfo, and its element-width calculation changes from a fixed minimum of 8 bits to the maximum of the target minimum and the active-bit-derived power-of-two width. The commit also adds the TargetTransformInfo forwarding API and a default TargetTransformInfoImpl hook returning 8.

Summary: Adds an LSR search-space narrowing heuristic that, when estimated complexity reaches the configured limit, merges an LSR use whose fixups are entirely outside the loop into a compatible in-loop use and deletes the original use. The commit also adds AArch64 and X86 regression coverage, including cases where outside-loop fixups must not be merged because they would create invalid offsets or formulae.
Changed symbols: LSRInstance::NarrowSearchSpaceByMergingUsesOutsideLoop; LSRInstance::NarrowSearchSpaceUsingHeuristics; LSRInstance; invalid_offset_outside_loop; illegal_formula_after_merge
Behavioral change: Invokes a new narrowing stage from LSR's heuristic search-space reduction.; Only runs when EstimateSearchSpaceComplexity() is at least ComplexityLimit.; Moves fixups from an all-outside-loop LSRUse to a compatible in-loop LSRUse, then deletes the former use.; Requires the outside-loop offsets to be legal for every candidate in-loop formula and requires matching initial formula components before merging.
Assertion or trace link: ClobberWalker::verifyOptResult; OtherClobbers; MSSA.dominates; MemorySSA.cpp; canHoistLoad; hoistRegion
Reproducer link: The added X86 test documents a separate LoopStrengthReduce assertion risk from merging outside-loop fixups with incompatible offsets.; No retrieved test runs the reported clang -O1 MemorySSA clobber-walker reproducer or checks the reported OtherClobbers dominance assertion.
Pass or subsystem link: LoopStrengthReduce; loop optimization; MemorySSA-backed LICM in the reported trace
Causal explanation: This commit changes loop pointer-expression rewriting, and its new tests demonstrate that incorrect merging can produce invalid LSR formulae. However, the retrieved implementation neither touches MemorySSA nor MemorySSAUpdater, and LoopStrengthReduce is not named in the supplied failing stack. The reported assertion occurs while MemorySSA's clobber walker is used by LICM, so the link is only indirect through a possible change in loop memory/address IR if this LSR path runs.
Causal confidence: 0.09
Build risk: Adds target-specific LSR regression tests for X86 and AArch64.; The new heuristic mutates the Uses collection while iterating and adjusts both the index and use count after DeleteUse.; The tests explicitly cover offset/formula legality and an assertion-prone outside-loop merge case.

diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopStrengthReduce/X86/use-outside-loop-crash.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopStrengthReduce/X86/use-outside-loop-crash.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..2fdee2ae94e9
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopStrengthReduce/X86/use-outside-loop-crash.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,165 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --version 6
+; RUN: opt -mtriple=x86_64 -loop-reduce -S < %s | FileCheck %s
+
+declare i1 @otherfn(ptr)
+
+; The use of %ptr in %gep outside the loop uses a fixup of 8 which is
+; incompatible with the use inside the loop as an argument to a call. We
+; therefore can't merge the two, as it would cause an assertion failure.
+
+define i64 @invalid_offset_outside_loop(ptr %ptr.arg, i64 %iv.arg) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define i64 @invalid_offset_outside_loop(
+; CHECK-SAME: ptr [[PTR_ARG:%.*]], i64 [[IV_ARG:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP0:%.*]] = add i64 [[IV_ARG]], -2
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[LOOP:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[LOOP]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[LSR_IV:%.*]] = phi i64 [ [[LSR_IV_NEXT:%.*]], %[[LOOP_INC:.*]] ], [ [[TMP0]], %[[ENTRY]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[PTR:%.*]] = phi ptr [ [[PTR_ARG]], %[[ENTRY]] ], [ [[PTR_NEXT:%.*]], %[[LOOP_INC]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CALL:%.*]] = call i1 @otherfn(ptr [[PTR]])
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CALL]], label %[[EXIT:.*]], label %[[LOOP_INC]]
+; CHECK:       [[LOOP_INC]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[PTR_NEXT]] = getelementptr i8, ptr [[PTR]], i64 16
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[LSR_IV_NEXT]] = add i64 [[LSR_IV]], -1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND:%.*]] = icmp eq i64 [[LSR_IV_NEXT]], -3
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND]], label %[[EXIT]], label %[[LOOP]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP1:%.*]] = add i64 [[LSR_IV]], 2
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP1:%.*]] = icmp slt i64 [[TMP1]], [[IV_ARG]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP2:%.*]] = icmp eq i64 [[LSR_IV]], -1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SEL1:%.*]] = select i1 [[CMP1]], i64 1, i64 2
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SEL2:%.*]] = select i1 [[CMP2]], i64 [[SEL1]], i64 3
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP:%.*]] = getelementptr i8, ptr [[PTR]], i64 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i64 [[SEL2]], ptr [[GEP]], align 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i64 [[LSR_IV]]
+;
+entry:
+  br label %loop
+
+loop:
+  %ptr = phi ptr [ %ptr.arg, %entry ], [ %ptr.next, %loop.inc ]
+  %iv = phi i64 [ %iv.arg, %entry ], [ %iv.next, %loop.inc ]
+  %call = call i1 @otherfn(ptr %ptr)
+  br i1 %call, label %exit, label %loop.inc
+
+loop.inc:
+  %ptr.next = getelementptr i8, ptr %ptr, i64 16
+  %iv.next = add i64 %iv, -1
+  %exitcond = icmp eq i64 %iv, 0
+  br i1 %exitcond, label %exit, label %loop
+
+exit:
+  %cmp1 = icmp slt i64 %iv, %iv.arg
+  %cmp2 = icmp eq i64 %iv, 1
+  %sel1 = select i1 %cmp1, i64 1, i64 2
+  %sel2 = select i1 %cmp2, i64 %sel1, i64 3
+  %gep = getelementptr i8, ptr %ptr, i64 8
+  store i64 %sel2, ptr %gep, align 8
+  %sub = add i64 %iv, -2
+  ret i64 %sub
+}
+
+; Stream 0 has two in-loop loads at relative offsets {-2^30, 0}, which makes
+; GenerateConstantOffsets produce formulae with BaseOffset +2^30. The exit
+; block loads at +1.5*2^30 past the post-inc pointer; x86 accepts that as a
+; disp32, so the merge gate isLegalUse(LU.MinOffset, LU.MaxOffset, ...,
+; Formulae[0]) passes, but 2^30 + 1.5*2^30 = 2.5*2^30 does not fit in a
+; signed 32-bit displacement, so the +2^30 formulae become illegal once the
+; outside-loop fixup is merged in. The test is sized so that the merge itself
+; drops EstimateSearchSpaceComplexity() below ComplexityLimit, so no later
+; narrowing step deletes the now-illegal formulae before Solve().
+
+define i32 @illegal_formula_after_merge(ptr %p, i64 %n) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define i32 @illegal_formula_after_merge(
+; CHECK-SAME: ptr [[P:%.*]], i64 [[N:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[P0_LOAD:%.*]] = load ptr, ptr [[P]], align 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[ARRAYIDX1:%.*]] = getelementptr ptr, ptr [[P]], i64 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[P1_LOAD:%.*]] = load ptr, pt

Summary: Extends SROA's tree-structured vector merge rewrite from a stores-only pattern to an initialization-plus-read-modify-write pattern. The new path recognizes a full initialization store followed by partial loads and stores, constrains relevant accesses to one block for ordering, initializes per-slice SSA values from the init store, and emits merged vector values while retaining checks that reject unsupported layouts and ordering cases.
Changed symbols: ReplaceFullLoad; TreeMerge; StoreInfo; LoadInfo; SROA tree-structured merge rewrite; coverage_gap; single_round; multi_round
Behavioral change: Classifies tree-merge candidates as either stores-only or init-plus-RMW patterns.; Adds same-basic-block checks for partial stores and, for RMW, the initialization store and partial loads so ordering can be represented without PHIs.; For stores-only candidates, sorts store ranges and requires exact tiling of the alloca before merging.; For RMW candidates, derives initial per-slice values from the full initialization store and tracks slice values in SSA.; Replaces a full-width load with a typed load from the merged alloca and uses a bitcast when the replacement load type differs.; Places generated merge instructions after the relevant stores or before the full load to avoid invalid SSA ordering.

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This GVN change alters where AvailableValue::MaterializeAdjustedValue inserts a rematerialized select: instead of inserting relative to the original SelectInst, it inserts at the caller-provided InsertPt. The accompanying GVN PRE test expectation updates move the materialized value select accordingly in loop/select cases.
Changed symbols: llvm::gvn::AvailableValue::MaterializeAdjustedValue; llvm::SelectInst::Create; GVN PRE checks in pre-loop-load-through-select.ll
Behavioral change: A rematerialized select is now inserted before InsertPt rather than before the source SelectInst.; This changes the resulting IR instruction placement and potentially the dominance/order of the newly materialized non-memory select in GVN PRE transformations.; The selected tests update expected placement of the materialized select in loop-based pointer/select load cases.
Assertion or trace link: MemorySSA::ClobberWalkerBase::getClobberingMemoryAccessBase; ClobberWalker::verifyOptResult; MemorySSA.cpp
Reproducer link: The issue is an -O1 assertion during MemorySSA clobber-walker verification.; The retrieved tests exercise GVN PRE on loop-carried pointer selects and loads, but do not reproduce the reported assertion.
Pass or subsystem link: GVN; GVN PRE; MemorySSA clobber walker (not directly modified)
Causal explanation: The patch changes generated IR placement in a scalar optimization that handles loads and loop-carried selects, so it could indirectly alter later optimizer input. However, the changed instruction is a select rather than a memory access, no MemorySSA or MemorySSAUpdater code is modified, and the supplied crash trace identifies LICM/MemorySSA clobber-walker activity rather than GVN. The evidence therefore supports only a weak indirect connection.
Causal confidence: 0.18
Build risk: Production compiler source is modified in llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar/GVN.cpp.; Existing GVN PRE regression checks were updated to reflect changed IR placement.; No MemorySSA-specific regression test or assertion reproducer is added in the retrieved hunks.

Summary: This ConstantHoisting fix avoids considering PHI operands whose incoming edge originates in a basic block unreachable from function entry. It uses DominatorTree reachability during candidate collection, preventing constant-hoisting/rebasing logic from processing those edges, and converts an existing crashing X86 test into a passing regression while adding an AArch64 unreachable-PHI-edge test.
Changed symbols: ConstantHoistingPass::collectConstantCandidates; func_29; func
Behavioral change: When scanning an instruction operand that belongs to a PHINode, obtains the corresponding incoming block.; Skips candidate analysis for that operand when DominatorTree reports the PHI incoming block is unreachable from entry.; Avoids the prior ConstantHoisting assertion scenario involving incomplete rebasing/update accounting for constants on unreachable PHI edges.
Assertion or trace link: The reported assertion is a MemorySSA ClobberWalker::verifyOptResult dominance check over OtherClobbers.; This change uses DominatorTree reachability and explicitly handles unreachable PHI predecessors, which is conceptually related to CFG reachability and dominance.; The retrieved hunk does not modify MemorySSA, MemorySSAUpdater, ClobberWalker, or MSSA.dominates, and ConstantHoisting is not named in the supplied pass tokens or stack.
Reproducer link: The added tests reproduce ConstantHoisting failures caused by unreachable PHI incoming edges and verify that the transformation now completes.; No supplied evidence shows that the pr204559 testcase has unreachable PHI edges or executes ConstantHoisting before the MemorySSA assertion.
Pass or subsystem link: ConstantHoisting; DominatorTree reachability; MemorySSA clobber-walker verification
Causal explanation: This is the closest candidate to a general CFG/dominance concern because it changes handling of unreachable PHI predecessors using DominatorTree reachability. Nevertheless, it only suppresses ConstantHoisting candidate processing, rather than updating CFG, MemorySSA, or MemorySSA dominance relations. The reported failure occurs in LICM's MemorySSA clobber query, so the retrieved evidence supports only a weak indirect relationship.
Causal confidence: 0.11
Build risk: The implementation relies on the existing DominatorTree pointer and its isReachableFromEntry query.; An existing assertion/crash-oriented X86 test is converted into a normal passing FileCheck test.; A new AArch64 regression test covers unreachable PHI incoming edges; the existing X86 test explicitly invokes an x86_64 target triple.

@@ -0,0 +1,58 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --version 6
+; RUN: opt < %s -mtriple aarch64-- -passes=consthoist -S | FileCheck %s
+
+; The PHI node has some inbound edges with constants that originate from
+; basic blocks that aren't reachable from entry. Those could be tricky
+; to update when trying to find insertion points etc for a common base
+; constant.
+
+; The test case was added as a regression test to show that that we no longer
+; hit assertion failures about number of users updated/rebased. The workaround
+; is to ignore phi edges from basic blocks that aren't reachable from entry
+; when looking for candidate constants.
+
+define i64 @func(i1 %b0, i1 %b1) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define i64 @func(
+; CHECK-SAME: i1 [[B0:%.*]], i1 [[B1:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*:]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[B0]], label %[[BLOCK1:.*]], label %[[BLOCK2:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[BLOCK1]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CONST1:%.*]] = bitcast i64 4886718345 to i64
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[MERGE:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[BLOCK2]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[B1]], label %[[BLOCK3:.*]], label %[[MERGE]]
+; CHECK:       [[BLOCK3]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CONST:%.*]] = bitcast i64 4886718345 to i64
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[MERGE]]
+; CHECK:       [[UNREACHABLE1:.*]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[MERGE]]
+; CHECK:       [[UNREACHABLE2:.*]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[MERGE]]
+; CHECK:       [[MERGE]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[V:%.*]] = phi i64 [ 4886718345, %[[UNREACHABLE1]] ], [ 4886718345, %[[UNREACHABLE2]] ], [ [[CONST1]], %[[BLOCK1]] ], [ [[CONST]], %[[BLOCK3]] ], [ 0, %[[BLOCK2]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i64 [[V]]
+;
+entry:
+  br i1 %b0, label %block1, label %block2
+
+block1:
+  br label %merge
+
+block2:
+  br i1 %b1, label %block3, label %merge
+
+block3:
+  br label %merge
+
+unreachable1:
+  br label %merge
+
+unreachable2:
+  br label %merge
+
+merge:
+  %v = phi i64 [ 4886718345, %unreachable1 ], [ 4886718345, %unreachable2 ], [ 4886718345, %block1 ], [ 4886718345, %block3 ], [ 0, %block2 ]
+  ret i64 %v
+}
+

top_candidates.subject: [Loads][NFC] Add isDereferenceablePointer overload taking a size (#203905)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This NFC refactoring adds a size-based isDereferenceablePointer overload and migrates several callers from isDereferenceableAndAlignedPointer(..., Align(1), Size, ...). The new overload directly delegates to the prior aligned query with Align(1), preserving the prior dereferenceability predicate while making the alignment-one use explicit.
Changed symbols: llvm::isDereferenceablePointer(const Value *, const APInt &, const SimplifyQuery &, bool); InstCombinerImpl::visitCallInst; MemCpyOptPass::performCallSlotOptzn; canTransformToMemCmp; BCECmpChain::isDereferenceable
Behavioral change: Introduces a public APInt-size dereferenceability query equivalent to isDereferenceableAndAlignedPointer with Align(1).; Changes InstCombine, MemCpyOptimizer, SimplifyLibCalls, and MergeICmps callers to invoke the new alignment-one wrapper.; The shown wrapper implementation delegates directly to the old predicate with identical Size, SimplifyQuery, IgnoreFree, and Align(1) inputs, so the retrieved code indicates no intended semantic change.
Assertion or trace link: The supplied assertion is in MemorySSA.cpp in ClobberWalker::verifyOptResult and concerns MSSA.dominates for OtherClobbers.; InstCombine and memcpyopt occur among the reported O1 pass tokens.; No retrieved hunk changes MemorySSA, ClobberWalker, MemorySSAUpdater, or a MemorySSA use/def update.
Reproducer link: No testcase details establish that dereferenceability reasoning, memcpy call-slot optimization, merged icmps, or libcalls simplification is required to reproduce the assertion.; The retrieved change contains no regression test hunk for the reported MemorySSA assertion.
Pass or subsystem link: Analysis/Loads dereferenceability reasoning; InstCombine; MemCpyOptimizer; MemorySSA clobber-walker verification
Causal explanation: There is a weak pipeline-level connection because InstCombine and memcpyopt are reported O1 passes, and these optimizations can use dereferenceability facts. However, every shown migration replaces an Align(1) call with a wrapper that immediately makes the same Align(1) call, and no MemorySSA state or dominance behavior is changed. The evidence therefore supports this as a low-likelihood cause of a MemorySSA clobber ordering assertion.
Causal confidence: 0.08
Build risk: The new public overload has a matching declaration in Loads.h and definition in Loads.cpp.; Multiple callers are migrated consistently to the new overload.; No dedicated test update is present in the retrieved hunks, so validation evidence is limited to the exact forwarding implementation and caller substitutions.

evidence: SimplifyCFG is explicitly present in the O1 pipeline and this change can newly speculate loads across CFG structure using contextual assumptions.

selection.diff_summary:
Summary: SimplifyCFG makes foldBranchToCommonDest context-aware when deciding whether instructions may be speculated: it derives a context instruction from the sole predecessor terminator and passes that context plus AssumptionCache to isSafeToSpeculativelyExecute. New tests cover branch folding with loads justified by dereferenceable attributes or assumptions.
Changed symbols: llvm::foldBranchToCommonDest; llvm::SimplifyCFGOpt::simplifyCondBranch; isSafeToSpeculativelyExecute; AssumptionCache; llvm/test/Transforms/SimplifyCFG/fold-branch-to-common-dest.ll
Behavioral change: foldBranchToCommonDest now supplies a context instruction when there is exactly one predecessor, using that predecessor's terminator as CxtI.; Speculation safety now also receives AssumptionCache, allowing the safety decision to use context-sensitive assumptions.; The transformation's willingness to speculatively move instructions, including loads, can therefore differ when dereferenceability is known from an argument attribute or a preceding llvm.assume.
Assertion or trace link: simplifycfg is explicitly present in the reported -O1 pass pipeline.; The reported failure is a later MemorySSA ClobberWalker::verifyOptResult dominance assertion.; The retrieved caller invokes foldBranchToCommonDest with MSSAU set to nullptr; no visible hunk performs a MemorySSA update.
Reproducer link: New tests specifically exercise speculative load placement under dereferenceable attributes and llvm.assume facts.; These tests demonstrate changed CFG/instruction-placement behavior, but do not contain the reported assertion or a MemorySSA verifier test.
Pass or subsystem link: SimplifyCFG; Speculative execution safety; AssumptionCache; Control-flow simplification
Causal explanation: This commit directly affects a pass that runs in the failing -O1 pipeline and can move loads across CFG structure based on contextual assumptions. Such IR changes can influence MemorySSA's later clobber reasoning. top_candidates.subject: [InstCombine] Fold X == Identity ? Y : min/max(X, Y) (#202748)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: Adds an InstructionSimplify fold for min/max intrinsics when operand replacement turns either operand into that intrinsic's identity value. The fold returns the other operand, dropping poison-generating annotations only when the caller permits flag dropping. InstCombine tests were added for signed and unsigned min/max identity cases, including commuted operands, negative cases, and range-annotation handling.
Changed symbols: llvm::simplifyWithOpsReplaced; llvm::MinMaxIntrinsic::getIdentity; select_signed_max_smin; select_npos_umin; select_not_npos_umin; select_npos_umin_commuted; select_npos_wrong_bound_negative; select_npos_umin_drop_range
Behavioral change: After replacing an instruction's operands, simplifyWithOpsReplaced recognizes MinMaxIntrinsic operands equal to the intrinsic identity and simplifies the min/max result to the non-identity operand.; The simplification refuses to remove poison-generating annotations unless DropFlags is available, in which case it records the intrinsic whose flags must be dropped.; The added InstCombine tests establish that select expressions guarding min/max identity values are folded to the underlying min/max call, while a select with a different replacement value is retained.
Assertion or trace link: InstCombine; MemorySSA::ClobberWalkerBase::getClobberingMemoryAccessBase; ClobberWalker::verifyOptResult; MSSA.dominates; OtherClobbers
Reproducer link: The reported failure occurs during an -O1 pipeline that includes InstCombine before loop-MSSA/LICM.; No retrieved hunk contains the reduced C reproducer or a MemorySSA verification test.
Pass or subsystem link: InstructionSimplify; InstCombine; MemorySSA/LICM only through later pipeline reachability
Causal explanation: This is directly in the InstCombine-related simplification path present in the failing pipeline, so it can change IR reaching later MemorySSA users. However, the visible change only folds pure min/max/select value expressions and does not create, remove, move, or update memory accesses, CFG edges, MemorySSA nodes, or dominance information. The retrieved evidence therefore provides only an indirect path to the later ClobberWalker dominance assertion.
Causal confidence: 0.18

Summary: SimpleLoopUnswitch generalizes trivial unswitching to handle a loop-invariant branch whose one successor is the loop latch, provided the latch is side-effect-free, the unique latch exit has loop-invariant PHIs, and ScalarEvolution proves the loop finite. It rewires that latch edge to the unique latch-exit block, repairs exit PHIs, and applies corresponding CFG updates through MemorySSAUpdater when available.

Behavioral change: A branch from within a loop to its latch can now be treated as trivially unswitchable when its other successor remains in the loop and the latch can safely be bypassed.; The transformation deletes the branch-to-latch CFG edge, inserts an edge from the branch block to the unique latch exit, removes the old predecessor from the latch, redirects the branch successor, and adds matching incoming values to unique-latch-exit PHIs.; It applies the CFG edge updates through MSSAU->applyUpdates(Updates, DT) when MemorySSAUpdater is available, otherwise through DT.applyUpdates(Updates).; The ordinary loop-exit-PHI invariant check is skipped after this special branch rewrite, with an assertion requiring that a modified branch must subsequently be unswitched.

It rewires that latch edge to the unique latch-exit block, repairs exit PHIs, and applies corresponding CFG updates through MemorySSAUpdater when available.
behavioral_change: A branch from within a loop to its latch can now be treated as trivially unswitchable when its other successor remains in the loop and the latch can safely be bypassed.

The transformation deletes the branch-to-latch CFG edge, inserts an edge from the branch block to the unique latch exit, removes the old predecessor from the latch, redirects the branch successor, and adds matching incoming values to unique-latch-exit PHIs.
It applies the CFG edge updates through MSSAU->applyUpdates(Updates, DT) when MemorySSAUpdater is available, otherwise through DT.applyUpdates(Updates).
The ordinary loop-exit-PHI invariant check is skipped after this special branch rewrite, with an assertion requiring that a modified branch must subsequently be unswitched.

assertion_or_trace: simple-loop-unswitch is explicitly listed in the failing -O1 pass pipeline.
The assertion is in MemorySSA::ClobberWalkerBase::verifyOptResult and requires every OtherClobber to dominate the PrimaryClobber.
This commit directly invokes MemorySSAUpdater::applyUpdates while changing CFG edges and dominance-relevant predecessor/PHI structure.
reproducer: The new trivial-unswitch test exercises precisely the new latch-bypass CFG rewrite in a perfect loop nest.
The phase-ordering O1 test changes expected loop CFG and retains loads/stores in the transformed nested-loop structure, showing that the change affects memory-bearing O1 IR.
The cold-function test distinguishes nontrivial duplication-based unswitching from the newly generalized nonduplicating trivial form.
issue_link.explanation: This is a strong candidate because it runs in the reported pipeline and performs a new CFG rewrite that explicitly updates both dominance information and MemorySSA. The reported verifier failure is specifically a dominance ordering violation among MemorySSA clobbers, so an incorrect or incomplete update after deleting the branch-to-latch edge and creating the branch-to-exit edge could plausibly produce the observed invalid clobber relation. The hunks do not prove that this transformation triggers on the supplied C testcase or that its updater call is defective, but they establish a direct mechanism matching the failing subsystem and invariant.

build_risk: The change introduces new control-flow rewriting, PHI repair, dominance updates, and conditional MemorySSAUpdater updates in a loop transform.
Correctness depends on several guards: unique latch exit, loop-invariant exit PHIs, no latch side effects, and a computable finite maximum backedge count.
New extensive SimpleLoopUnswitch and phase-ordering tests cover the added behavior, including an O1 output change involving nested loops and memory operations.
The branch-rewrite path has an explicit assertion that it must lead to successful unswitching, indicating a newly constrained transformation state.

+
+;; Check that genuinely non-trivial loop unswitching - where the optimizer
+;; would have to duplicate the entire loop body - is suppressed for cold
+;; (optsize/minsize) functions.
+;;
+;; The branch on %cond in the loop header is loop-invariant, but both of its
+;; successors (if.then, if.else) stay inside the loop, so unswitching it
+;; requires producing two full copies of the loop.  That code-size increase
+;; must be blocked when the function is cold.
+;;
+;; Contrast with unswitch-cold-func.ll, where the invariant condition can be
+;; hoisted via a latch-bypass rewrite that introduces no code duplication and
+;; is therefore allowed even for cold functions.
+;;
+;; Source:
+;;   void function(bool cond, int N, int *A, int *B) {
+;;     for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
+;;       if (cond) A[i]++;
+;;       else      B[i]++;
+;;     }
+;;   }
+;; profiled when called with N=0 (cold).
+
+define void @function(i1 %cond, i32 %N, ptr %A, ptr %B) !prof !16 {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @function
+; CHECK-SAME: (i1 [[COND:%.*]], i32 [[N:%.*]], ptr [[A:%.*]], ptr [[B:%.*]]) #[[ATTR0:[0-9]+]] {{.*}}{
+; CHECK-NEXT:  entry:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_NOT:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[N]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_NOT]], label [[EXIT:%.*]], label [[LOOP_PREHEADER:%.*]], !prof [[PROF17:![0-9]+]]
+; CHECK:       loop.preheader:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_HEADER:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       loop.header:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, [[LOOP_PREHEADER]] ], [ [[I_NEXT:%.*]], [[LOOP_LATCH:%.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[COND]], label [[IF_THEN:%.*]], label [[IF_ELSE:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       if.then:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_A:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[A]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL_A:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC_A:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL_A]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC_A]], ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       if.else:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_B:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[B]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL_B:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC_B:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL_B]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC_B]], ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       loop.latch:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[I]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_NOT:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[I_NEXT]], [[N]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_NOT]], label [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT:%.*]], label [[LOOP_HEADER]], !prof [[PROF17]]
+; CHECK:       exit.loopexit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[EXIT]]
+; CHECK:       exit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %cmp.not = icmp sle i32 %N, 0
+  br i1 %cmp.not, label %exit, label %loop.preheader, !prof !17
+
+loop.preheader:
+  br label %loop.header
+
+loop.header:
+  %i = phi i32 [ 0, %loop.preheader ], [ %i.next, %loop.latch ]
+  br i1 %cond, label %if.then, label %if.else
+
+if.then:
+  %gep.a = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %A, i32 %i
+  %val.a = load i32, ptr %gep.a, align 4
+  %inc.a = add i32 %val.a, 1
+  store i32 %inc.a, ptr %gep.a, align 4
+  br label %loop.latch
+
+if.else:
+  %gep.b = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %B, i32 %i
+  %va

index 000000000000..d08c03e7a31f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/SimpleLoopUnswitch/trivial-unswitch-loop-guard.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,1031 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --version 6
+; RUN: opt -passes='loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch),verify<loops>' -S < %s | FileCheck %s
+
+;; Check that a loop-invariant guard branch in a perfect nest is trivially
+;; unswitched.  The outer loop's header branches to the latch (skipping the
+;; inner loop entirely) when N == 0, or falls through into the inner loop.
+;; Because N is loop-invariant, the new code in unswitchTrivialBranch rewires
+;; the latch arm to point at the outer-loop exit, making the branch look like
+;; an ordinary exit branch and allowing the standard trivial-unswitch logic to
+;; hoist it out of the outer loop.
+;;
+;; Source:
+;;   void f(int M, int N, int *A, int *B) {
+;;     for (int j = 0; j < M; j++) {
+;;       if (N <= 0) continue;          // invariant guard branches to latch
+;;       for (int i = 0; i < N; i++)
+;;         A[i] = B[i] + 1;
+;;     }
+;;   }
+;; The key CFG edge is: outer.header --[N==0]--> outer.latch (the latch),
+;; outer.header --[N!=0]--> inner.preheader (inside the outer loop).
+
+define void @perfect_nest_guard(i32 %M, i32 %N, ptr %A, ptr %B) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @perfect_nest_guard(
+; CHECK-SAME: i32 [[M:%.*]], i32 [[N:%.*]], ptr [[A:%.*]], ptr [[B:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*:]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_M:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[M]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_M]], label %[[EXIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_PREHEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_PREHEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GUARD:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[N]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[GUARD]], label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[OUTER_HEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_HEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[J:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, %[[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT]] ], [ [[J_NEXT:%.*]], %[[OUTER_LATCH:.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_PREHEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_PREHEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_HEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_HEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, %[[INNER_PREHEADER]] ], [ [[I_NEXT:%.*]], %[[INNER_LATCH:.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_B:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[B]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_A:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[A]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC]], ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_LATCH]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[I]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_INNER:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[I_NEXT]], [[N]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_INNER]], label %[[OUTER_LATCH_LOOPEXIT:.*]], label %[[INNER_HEADER]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_LATCH_LOOPEXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[OUTER_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_LATCH]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[J_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[J]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_OUTER:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[J_NEXT]], [[M]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_OUTER]], label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_HEADER]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[EXIT]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %cmp.M = icmp sle i32 %M, 0
+  br i1 %cmp.M, label %exit, label %outer.preheader
+
+outer.preheader:
+  %guard = icmp sle i32 %N, 0
+  br label %outer.header
+
+outer.header:
+  %j = phi i32 [ 0, %outer.preheader ], [ %j.next, %outer.latch ]
+  br i1 %guard, label %outer.latch,

Summary: Refactors intrinsic creation so callers that may receive a constant-folded result use Value* from CreateIntrinsic, while callers that require an actual CallInst or specific intrinsic instruction explicitly use CreateIntrinsicWithoutFolding. The visible changes adapt target InstCombine implementations and preserve concrete call creation for memset.inline, callbr landing-pad insertion, and AMDGPU intrinsic rewrites.
Changed symbols: llvm::IRBuilderBase::CreateMemSetInline; llvm::IRBuilderBase::CreateIntrinsic; llvm::IRBuilderBase::CreateIntrinsicWithoutFolding; GCNTTIImpl::instCombineIntrinsic; simplifyAMDGCNMemoryIntrinsicDemanded; modifyIntrinsicCall; instCombineSVEVectorFuseMulAddSub; insertIntrinsicCalls
Behavioral change: Intrinsic construction may now yield a folded Value rather than always a CallInst, requiring consumers that can accept folding to store the result as Value*.; Consumers that require a materialized call or a specific CallInst-derived type are switched to CreateIntrinsicWithoutFolding.; CreateMemSetInline explicitly uses non-folding intrinsic creation and casts the resulting value to MemSetInst, preserving the requirement that this helper produces a concrete memory-writing instruction.; The AMDGPU demanded-memory-intrinsic rewrite and InlineAsmPrepare callbr-lowering path explicitly retain concrete CallInst creation.
Assertion or trace link: InstCombine; MemorySSA::ClobberWalkerBase::getClobberingMemoryAccessBase; ClobberWalker::verifyOptResult; OtherClobbers; MSSA.dominates

Pass or subsystem link: IRBuilder intrinsic construction; AMDGPU and AArch64 InstCombine support; InlineAsmPrepare; MemorySSA only through possible downstream IR-shape effects

The retrieved code also specifically protects memory-affecting memset.inline creation with CreateIntrinsicWithoutFolding, reducing the likelihood that this visible path removes a MemorySSA-relevant access. No shown change modifies MemorySSA, MemorySSAUpdater, dominance maintenance, LICM, or the ClobberWalker invariant, and much of the visible InstCombine use is target-specific. Summary: This commit extends SimpleLoopUnswitch's "trivial" unswitching to handle an invariant conditional branch whose one successor is the loop latch and whose other successor remains in the loop. When strict safety conditions hold, it rewrites the branch-to-latch edge into an edge to the unique latch-exit block, repairs exit PHIs, updates either MemorySSA or the dominator tree, and then allows the normal trivial-unswitch path to proceed without rechecking the pre-rewrite exit-PHI condition.
Changed symbols: unswitchTrivialBranch; Loop::getLoopLatch; Loop::getUniqueLatchExitBlock; areLoopExitPHIsLoopInvariant; MemorySSAUpdater::applyUpdates; DominatorTree::applyUpdates
Behavioral change: Recognizes a new trivial-unswitch form where an invariant branch targets the loop latch on one arm and an in-loop block on the other, rather than requiring a successor that is already a loop exit.; Rewrites the CFG by deleting the branch-parent-to-latch edge and inserting a branch-parent-to-unique-latch-exit edge.; Removes the rewritten branch parent as a predecessor of the latch and adds corresponding incoming values to PHIs in the unique latch-exit block.; Applies the CFG edge updates through MemorySSAUpdater when MemorySSA is available, otherwise through DominatorTree.; Skips the existing loop-exit-PHI-invariance rejection after this new rewrite, guarded by the ModifiedBranch state.
Assertion or trace link: The failure is a MemorySSA ClobberWalker::verifyOptResult assertion over MSSA.dominates and OtherClobbers.; The changed code directly invokes MemorySSAUpdater::applyUpdates after changing CFG edges and predecessor/PHI structure.; The reported O1 pass sequence includes loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch), followed later by LICM, whose stack includes canHoistLoad and MemorySSA clobber walking.
Reproducer link: The reported crash occurs at -O1, and this commit changes O1 PhaseOrdering expectations in hoist-load-of-baseptr.ll.; The new SimpleLoopUnswitch test exercises loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch) on a perfect nested loop with loads and stores, including the newly supported latch-guard CFG shape.; No execution of the supplied pr204559 reduced testcase against this revision is provided.
Pass or subsystem link: SimpleLoopUnswitch; loop-mssa; MemorySSAUpdater; DominatorTree; LICM/MemorySSA clobber walking
Causal explanation: This is a strong candidate because it introduces a CFG and PHI rewrite in the exact SimpleLoopUnswitch stage present in the failing O1 pipeline, and explicitly relies on MemorySSAUpdater to preserve MemorySSA consistency. A missed or insufficient update for the new latch-to-exit transformation could leave MemorySSA dominance relationships inconsistent; a later LICM clobber-walker query could then trigger the reported verifyOptResult assertion. The retrieved evidence establishes this direct mechanism and pipeline ordering, but does not include a reproducer confirmation.

index 000000000000..6b84b45ef477
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/unswitch-nontrivial-cold-func.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,114 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --scrub-attributes --version 2
+
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes='pgo-force-function-attrs,function(loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch<nontrivial>))' -pgo-kind=pgo-instr-use-pipeline -pgo-cold-func-opt=optsize -S | FileCheck %s
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes='pgo-force-function-attrs,function(loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch<nontrivial>))' -pgo-kind=pgo-instr-use-pipeline -pgo-cold-func-opt=minsize -S | FileCheck %s
+
+;; Check that genuinely non-trivial loop unswitching - where the optimizer
+;; would have to duplicate the entire loop body - is suppressed for cold
+;; (optsize/minsize) functions.
+;;
+;; The branch on %cond in the loop header is loop-invariant, but both of its
+;; successors (if.then, if.else) stay inside the loop, so unswitching it
+;; requires producing two full copies of the loop.  That code-size increase
+;; must be blocked when the function is cold.
+;;
+;; Contrast with unswitch-cold-func.ll, where the invariant condition can be
+;; hoisted via a latch-bypass rewrite that introduces no code duplication and
+;; is therefore allowed even for cold functions.
+;;
+;; Source:
+;;   void function(bool cond, int N, int *A, int *B) {
+;;     for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
+;;       if (cond) A[i]++;
+;;       else      B[i]++;
+;;     }
+;;   }
+;; profiled when called with N=0 (cold).
+
+define void @function(i1 %cond, i32 %N, ptr %A, ptr %B) !prof !16 {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @function
+; CHECK-SAME: (i1 [[COND:%.*]], i32 [[N:%.*]], ptr [[A:%.*]], ptr [[B:%.*]]) #[[ATTR0:[0-9]+]] {{.*}}{
+; CHECK-NEXT:  entry:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_NOT:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[N]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_NOT]], label [[EXIT:%.*]], label [[LOOP_PREHEADER:%.*]], !prof [[PROF17:![0-9]+]]
+; CHECK:       loop.preheader:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_HEADER:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       loop.header:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, [[LOOP_PREHEADER]] ], [ [[I_NEXT:%.*]], [[LOOP_LATCH:%.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[COND]], label [[IF_THEN:%.*]], label [[IF_ELSE:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       if.then:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_A:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[A]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL_A:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC_A:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL_A]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC_A]], ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       if.else:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_B:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[B]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL_B:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC_B:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL_B]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC_B]], ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       loop.latch:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[I]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_NOT:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[I_NEXT]], [[N]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_NOT]], label [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT:%.*]], label [[LOOP_HEADER]], !prof [[PROF17]]
+; CHECK:       exit.loopexit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[EXIT]]
+; CHECK:       exit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %cmp.not = icmp sle i32 %N, 0
+  br i1 %cmp.not, label %exit, label %loop.preheader, !prof !17
+
+loop.preheader:
+  br label %loop.header
+
+loop.header:
+  %i = phi i32 [ 0, %loop.preheader ], [ %i.next, %loop.latch ]
+  br i1 %cond, label %if.then, label %if.else
+
+if.then:
+  %gep.a = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %A, i32 %i
+  %val.a = load i32, ptr %gep.a, align 4
+  %inc.a = add i32 %val.a, 1
+  store i32 %inc.a, ptr %gep.a, align 4
+  br label %loop.latch
+
+if.else:
+  %gep.b = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %B, i32 %i
+  %va

diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/SimpleLoopUnswitch/trivial-unswitch-loop-guard.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/SimpleLoopUnswitch/trivial-unswitch-loop-guard.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..d08c03e7a31f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/SimpleLoopUnswitch/trivial-unswitch-loop-guard.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,1031 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --version 6
+; RUN: opt -passes='loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch),verify<loops>' -S < %s | FileCheck %s
+
+;; Check that a loop-invariant guard branch in a perfect nest is trivially
+;; unswitched.  The outer loop's header branches to the latch (skipping the
+;; inner loop entirely) when N == 0, or falls through into the inner loop.
+;; Because N is loop-invariant, the new code in unswitchTrivialBranch rewires
+;; the latch arm to point at the outer-loop exit, making the branch look like
+;; an ordinary exit branch and allowing the standard trivial-unswitch logic to
+;; hoist it out of the outer loop.
+;;
+;; Source:
+;;   void f(int M, int N, int *A, int *B) {
+;;     for (int j = 0; j < M; j++) {
+;;       if (N <= 0) continue;          // invariant guard branches to latch
+;;       for (int i = 0; i < N; i++)
+;;         A[i] = B[i] + 1;
+;;     }
+;;   }
+;; The key CFG edge is: outer.header --[N==0]--> outer.latch (the latch),
+;; outer.header --[N!=0]--> inner.preheader (inside the outer loop).
+
+define void @perfect_nest_guard(i32 %M, i32 %N, ptr %A, ptr %B) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @perfect_nest_guard(
+; CHECK-SAME: i32 [[M:%.*]], i32 [[N:%.*]], ptr [[A:%.*]], ptr [[B:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*:]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_M:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[M]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_M]], label %[[EXIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_PREHEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_PREHEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GUARD:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[N]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[GUARD]], label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[OUTER_HEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_HEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[J:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, %[[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT]] ], [ [[J_NEXT:%.*]], %[[OUTER_LATCH:.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_PREHEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_PREHEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_HEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_HEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, %[[INNER_PREHEADER]] ], [ [[I_NEXT:%.*]], %[[INNER_LATCH:.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_B:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[B]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_A:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[A]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC]], ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_LATCH]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[I]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_INNER:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[I_NEXT]], [[N]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_INNER]], label %[[OUTER_LATCH_LOOPEXIT:.*]], label %[[INNER_HEADER]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_LATCH_LOOPEXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[OUTER_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_LATCH]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[J_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[J]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_OUTER:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[J_NEXT]], [[M]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_OUTER]], label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_HEADER]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[EXIT]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %cmp.M = icmp sle i32 %M, 0
+  br i1 %cmp.M, label %exit, label %outer.preheader
+
+outer.preheader:
+  %guard = icmp sle i32 %N, 0
+  br label %outer.header
+
+outer.header:
+  %j = phi i32 [ 0, %outer.preheader ], [ %j.next, %outer.latch ]
+  br i1 %guard, label %outer.latch,

Summary: This commit extends SimpleLoopUnswitch's "trivial" unswitching to handle an invariant conditional branch whose one successor is the loop latch and whose other successor remains in the loop. When strict safety conditions hold, it rewrites the branch-to-latch edge into an edge to the unique latch-exit block, repairs exit PHIs, updates either MemorySSA or the dominator tree, and then allows the normal trivial-unswitch path to proceed without rechecking the pre-rewrite exit-PHI condition.
Changed symbols: unswitchTrivialBranch; Loop::getLoopLatch; Loop::getUniqueLatchExitBlock; areLoopExitPHIsLoopInvariant; MemorySSAUpdater::applyUpdates; DominatorTree::applyUpdates
Behavioral change: Recognizes a new trivial-unswitch form where an invariant branch targets the loop latch on one arm and an in-loop block on the other, rather than requiring a successor that is already a loop exit.; Rewrites the CFG by deleting the branch-parent-to-latch edge and inserting a branch-parent-to-unique-latch-exit edge.; Removes the rewritten branch parent as a predecessor of the latch and adds corresponding incoming values to PHIs in the unique latch-exit block.; Applies the CFG edge updates through MemorySSAUpdater when MemorySSA is available, otherwise through DominatorTree.; Skips the existing loop-exit-PHI-invariance rejection after this new rewrite, guarded by the ModifiedBranch state.
Assertion or trace link: The failure is a MemorySSA ClobberWalker::verifyOptResult assertion over MSSA.dominates and OtherClobbers.; The changed code directly invokes MemorySSAUpdater::applyUpdates after changing CFG edges and predecessor/PHI structure.; The reported O1 pass sequence includes loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch), followed later by LICM, whose stack includes canHoistLoad and MemorySSA clobber walking.
Reproducer link: The reported crash occurs at -O1, and this commit changes O1 PhaseOrdering expectations in hoist-load-of-baseptr.ll.; The new SimpleLoopUnswitch test exercises loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch) on a perfect nested loop with loads and stores, including the newly supported latch-guard CFG shape.; No execution of the supplied pr204559 reduced testcase against this revision is provided.
Pass or subsystem link: SimpleLoopUnswitch; loop-mssa; MemorySSAUpdater; DominatorTree; LICM/MemorySSA clobber walking
Causal explanation: This is a strong candidate because it introduces a CFG and PHI rewrite in the exact SimpleLoopUnswitch stage present in the failing O1 pipeline, and explicitly relies on MemorySSAUpdater to preserve MemorySSA consistency. A missed or insufficient update for the new latch-to-exit transformation could leave MemorySSA dominance relationships inconsistent; a later LICM clobber-walker query could then trigger the reported verifyOptResult assertion. The retrieved evidence establishes this direct mechanism and pipeline ordering, but does not include a reproducer confirmation.
Causal confidence: 0.79
Build risk: The implementation uses the optional MemorySSAUpdater path and a DominatorTree fallback, so correctness depends on both CFG-update representations matching the actual predecessor and PHI mutations.; New coverage runs loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch), and one test also runs verify<loops>, but the visible tests do not run a MemorySSA verifier after the transformation.; Adjusted O1 PhaseOrdering checks demonstrate pipeline-visible CFG changes beyond the dedicated unswitch tests.

diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/unswitch-nontrivial-cold-func.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/unswitch-nontrivial-cold-func.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..6b84b45ef477
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/unswitch-nontrivial-cold-func.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,114 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --scrub-attributes --version 2
+
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes='pgo-force-function-attrs,function(loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch<nontrivial>))' -pgo-kind=pgo-instr-use-pipeline -pgo-cold-func-opt=optsize -S | FileCheck %s
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes='pgo-force-function-attrs,function(loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch<nontrivial>))' -pgo-kind=pgo-instr-use-pipeline -pgo-cold-func-opt=minsize -S | FileCheck %s
+
+;; Check that genuinely non-trivial loop unswitching - where the optimizer
+;; would have to duplicate the entire loop body - is suppressed for cold
+;; (optsize/minsize) functions.
+;;
+;; The branch on %cond in the loop header is loop-invariant, but both of its
+;; successors (if.then, if.else) stay inside the loop, so unswitching it
+;; requires producing two full copies of the loop.  That code-size increase
+;; must be blocked when the function is cold.
+;;
+;; Contrast with unswitch-cold-func.ll, where the invariant condition can be
+;; hoisted via a latch-bypass rewrite that introduces no code duplication and
+;; is therefore allowed even for cold functions.
+;;
+;; Source:
+;;   void function(bool cond, int N, int *A, int *B) {
+;;     for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
+;;       if (cond) A[i]++;
+;;       else      B[i]++;
+;;     }
+;;   }
+;; profiled when called with N=0 (cold).
+
+define void @function(i1 %cond, i32 %N, ptr %A, ptr %B) !prof !16 {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @function
+; CHECK-SAME: (i1 [[COND:%.*]], i32 [[N:%.*]], ptr [[A:%.*]], ptr [[B:%.*]]) #[[ATTR0:[0-9]+]] {{.*}}{
+; CHECK-NEXT:  entry:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_NOT:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[N]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_NOT]], label [[EXIT:%.*]], label [[LOOP_PREHEADER:%.*]], !prof [[PROF17:![0-9]+]]
+; CHECK:       loop.preheader:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_HEADER:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       loop.header:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, [[LOOP_PREHEADER]] ], [ [[I_NEXT:%.*]], [[LOOP_LATCH:%.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[COND]], label [[IF_THEN:%.*]], label [[IF_ELSE:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       if.then:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_A:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[A]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL_A:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC_A:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL_A]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC_A]], ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       if.else:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_B:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[B]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL_B:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC_B:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL_B]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC_B]], ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       loop.latch:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[I]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_NOT:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[I_NEXT]], [[N]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_NOT]], label [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT:%.*]], label [[LOOP_HEADER]], !prof [[PROF17]]
+; CHECK:       exit.loopexit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[EXIT]]
+; CHECK:       exit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %cmp.not = icmp sle i32 %N, 0
+  br i1 %cmp.not, label %exit, label %loop.preheader, !prof !17
+
+loop.preheader:
+  br label %loop.header
+
+loop.header:
+  %i = phi i32 [ 0, %loop.preheader ], [ %i.next, %loop.latch ]
+  br i1 %cond, label %if.then, label %if.else
+
+if.then:
+  %gep.a = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %A, i32 %i
+  %val.a = load i32, ptr %gep.a, align 4
+  %inc.a = add i32 %val.a, 1
+  store i32 %inc.a, ptr %gep.a, align 4
+  br label %loop.latch
+
+if.else:
+  %gep.b = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %B, i32 %i
+  %va
